Title: March 5, 2026 City of Boulder City Council Meeting - Regular Meeting

Topic1.Title: Open Comment: Flock Camera Contract and South Boulder Rec Center
Topic1.Summary: Numerous residents spoke against renewing the Flock surveillance camera contract, citing privacy concerns, data sharing with ICE, and Flock's record of broken promises. Many other speakers urged the council to preserve the South Boulder Rec Center, especially its pool and gymnasium, citing its importance for seniors, swim teams, youth, and walkability. Council members acknowledged the comments, and city staff said conversations about Flock and a facilities funding study session on April 9 are ongoing.

Topic2.Title: Consent Agenda and Area 3 Planning Reserve Resolution
Topic2.Summary: The council approved the consent agenda unanimously, with item 3E pulled for separate discussion. Council revised the Area 3 Planning Reserve resolution to broaden the housing types it contemplates, rather than focusing exclusively on middle-income ownership, and directed staff to bring back updated language. The council then passed the consent agenda minus item 3E.

Topic3.Title: Callup Check-In: Frontier Avenue Redevelopment Concept Plan
Topic3.Summary: The council reviewed a concept plan for redeveloping 3550 and 3850 Frontier Avenue with an events venue, hotel, about 500 apartments, and commercial space. Council members agreed that staff and the Planning Board had adequately reviewed the proposal and declined to call it up. Staff noted that a rezoning or tailored zone district would be needed and that council would weigh in during site review.

Topic4.Title: Public Hearing: 2026 Board and Commission Appointments
Topic4.Summary: Two speakers addressed the appointments during the public hearing, and the hearing was closed after one personal attack was ruled out of order. Council nominated and voted on candidates for vacant seats on numerous boards and commissions, including Arts Commission, Board of Zoning Adjustment, Boulder Urban Renewal Authority, Planning Board, and Housing Advisory Board. The council unanimously approved the 2026 appointments, with the Boulder Urban Renewal Authority appointments made effective immediately.

Topic5.Title: Review of Affordable Housing in Boulder
Topic5.Summary: Staff presented an overview of Boulder's affordable housing efforts, including the widening gap between area median income and home prices and projected rental and ownership shortfalls identified in the Dr. Cog study. The presentation highlighted local funding, inclusionary housing outperforming its 25% requirement, partnerships with nonprofits, and programs such as down payment assistance, scattered site acquisition, and Boulder Mod. Council members asked questions about cash-in-lieu payments, progress toward the 15% goal by 2035, underused down payment funds, and housing needs for seniors and low-income residents.
